devanagari:
बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्यात्मानं नियम्य च |
शब्दादीन्विषयांस्त्यक्त्वा रागद्वेषौ व्युदस्य च || ५१ ||
englishScript:
buddhyā viśuddhayā yukto dhṛtyātmānaṁ niyamya ca
śabdādīn viṣayāṁs tyaktvā rāga-dveṣau vyudasya ca (18.51)
translation: Endowed with a purified intellect, restraining the self with firm resolve, abandoning sense objects such as sound, and casting aside attraction and aversion...
sentences: Let us pull open the internal engine of the human decision-making mechanism and look closely at how a purified intellect, known as Vishuddha Buddhi, operates under real-life stress.
If you watch a muddy water glass settle, the dirt slowly sinks to the bottom until the water above becomes completely transparent.
In the exact same way, when your inner noisy thoughts quiet down, your core intellect stops getting clouded by immediate emotional impulses.
You begin to see reality as it actually is, rather than how your temporary fears or greedy cravings distort it.
This clarity requires Dhriti, which is the internal steering wheel of firm mental resolve that holds your attention steady.
Without Dhriti, your focus bounces around uncontrollably like a loose marble on a tilted glass table.
Notice how easily external sounds, sights, and physical sensations pull your mind out of its deep work alignment.
These external inputs are Vishaya, the sensory signals that constantly bombard your brain from the surrounding environment.
When you abandon automatic emotional reactions to Vishaya, you break the unconscious feedback loop of instant gratification.
Consider what happens when you feel a strong craving, which is Raga, or a powerful burning hatred, which is Dvesha.
Raga pulls you toward things with blind obsessive attraction, while Dvesha pushes you away with irrational panic and hostility.
Both Raga and Dvesha act like strong magnetic fields that throw off your internal compass of truth.
If you let those two forces run your life, you are basically operating on autopilot without any conscious control.
By casting aside Raga and Dvesha, you gain total command over your internal energy reserves.
Think of your mind as a high-powered lamp that shines brightest when protected from sudden gusts of wind.
When Vishuddha Buddhi is active, you no longer waste vital cognitive energy obsessing over momentary comfort or discomfort.
You observe sensory inputs coming in, but you choose not to let them trigger automatic internal drama.
This mental self-restraint is not forced suppression or painful self-torture.
Instead, it is a clean, natural state of clarity where you see through the illusion of short-term distractions.
Every single time you catch yourself reacting blindly to a sensory prompt, you can pause and re-center your intellect.
This disciplined practice builds an unshakeable foundation of inner mental stability.
You begin to realize that peace is not something you chase in the outside world, but a frequency you tune into internally.
As your mind becomes cleaner, your ability to make sharp, objective decisions increases dramatically.
You no longer confuse quick temporary pleasure with lasting long-term fulfillment.
This shift in awareness frees up massive bandwidth for deep creative focus and profound self-understanding.
You stop being a victim of external circumstance and become the master of your internal state.
The relentless urge to hunt for external validation simply dissolves into quiet inner confidence.
This is the first major step in cleaning up the lens through which you perceive reality.
By mastering this initial filter, you set the stage for deeper levels of self-mastery.
Your attention becomes a powerful laser beam rather than a scattered lightbulb.
This pure clarity paves the direct pathway toward absolute freedom and ultimate self-realization.

devanagari:
विविक्तसेवी लघ्वाशी यतवाक्कायमानसः |
ध्यानयोगपरो नित्यं वैराग्यं समुपाश्रितः || ५२ ||
englishScript:
vivikta-sevī laghv-āśī yata-vāk-kāya-mānasaḥ
dhyāna-yoga-paro nityaṁ vairāgyaṁ samupāśritaḥ (18.52)
translation: Dwelling in a quiet and secluded place, eating lightly, controlling speech, body, and mind, constantly engaged in meditation and yoga, and taking firm refuge in dispassion...
sentences: Now let us examine the physical and mental environment needed to sustain high-level internal clarity without draining your battery.
The concept of Vivikta-sevi means seeking out quiet, clutter-free spaces where your nervous system can finally drop its defensive noise.
Imagine trying to hear a delicate musical note while standing next to a roaring jet engine; that is what modern mental overstimulation does to your focus.
When you step into quiet solitude, your brain stops burning excess fuel on background threats and social performance.
Next comes Laghv-ashi, which is the practice of light, clean, and moderate physical consumption.
If you overfill an engine with heavy fuel, the motor bogs down, generates smoke, and loses its crisp responsiveness.
Similarly, overeating or consuming heavy junk foods dulls your sharpness and fills your system with sluggish Tamas.
Controlling your speech, body, and mental thoughts is described here as Yata-vak-kaya-manasa.
Your words, physical movements, and mental imaginations are three main pipes where your vital energy leaks out all day.
When you stop gossiping, eliminate nervous fidgeting, and quiet useless mental chatter, all that trapped energy gathers back inside you.
This conserved force is then channeled directly into Dhyana-yoga, the continuous practice of steady, deep meditation.
Dhyana-yoga is not sitting still with closed eyes while daydreaming about your next meal.
It is the systematic training of your attention to stay locked onto the ultimate truth of your inner observer.
To keep this meditation stable, you must take firm refuge in Vairagya, which means objective dispassion toward superficial shiny objects.
Vairagya is not cold emotional numbness or hating the world around you.
It is simply seeing through the temporal, passing nature of external sights, sounds, and social status.
When you realize that external objects cannot give you permanent security, your mental attachments naturally drop away.
Think of a scientist in a laboratory who stays completely objective while observing experiment data without getting emotionally hysterical.
That neutral, super-focused scientific attitude is the exact essence of Vairagya in daily life.
By living simply and eating light, your body remains energetic, light, and free from chronic physical fatigue.
By speaking only what is truthful and necessary, your words gain incredible weight and clarity.
By disciplining your thoughts, your mind transforms from a noisy battleground into a peaceful sanctuary.
This combination of quiet space, light diet, controlled energy, and steady dispassion builds an bulletproof internal sanctuary.
You are no longer pulled left and right by every random trend, opinion, or environmental distraction.
You master the art of being fully present in the world without letting the world mess up your internal calm.
This quiet lifestyle cleanses your internal hardware so that high-level spiritual insight can flow without resistance.
It turns your personal daily routine into an efficient laboratory for constant self-discovery.
You begin to experience a profound sense of inner independence that does not rely on external approval.
Your daily focus sharpens to a razor edge because unnecessary friction has been completely stripped away.
This disciplined lifestyle forms the quiet baseline for profound internal transformation.
It establishes the perfect conditions for breaking free from ego-driven limitations forever.

devanagari:
अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् |
विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते || ५३ ||
englishScript:
ahaṅkāraṁ balaṁ darpaṁ kāmaṁ krodhaṁ parigraham
vimucya nirmamaḥ śānto brahma-bhūyāya kalpate (18.53)
translation: Relinquishing egoism, raw physical force, arrogance, desire, anger, and acquisitiveness, free from possessiveness and serene, one becomes fit for realization of the Supreme Brahman.
sentences: Let us dissect the six major psychological heavy weights that drag down your consciousness and keep you trapped in anxiety.
The first weight is Ahankara, the false egoic identity that constantly shouts 'I am the center of everything.'
When Ahankara runs the show, every single event is filtered through self-centered vulnerability and fragile pride.
The second weight is Bala, which here refers to using aggressive physical or mental force to dominate and control others.
The third weight is Darpa, the foolish arrogance that makes you feel superior and untouchable compared to everyone else.
The fourth weight is Kama, the endless craving to possess more sensory pleasures and personal comforts.
When Kama is blocked or denied, it immediately mutates into Krodha, which is destructive, blinding anger.
The sixth weight is Parigraha, the obsessive hoarding of physical items and mental attachments you do not even need.
Imagine trying to swim across a deep ocean while carrying six heavy iron rocks tied tightly around your waist.
No matter how strong a swimmer you are, those six heavy burdens will pull you under the surface.
To become fit for Brahma-bhuyaya, which means establishing your identity in the infinite supreme reality, you must drop those weights.
Vimucya means completely unbuckling and releasing these toxic habits from your psychological structure.
When you release them, you attain the state of Nirmama, which means being entirely free from possessive 'mine-ness.'
Nirmama means you can use tools, enjoy homes, and build projects without foolishly believing you own them eternally.
You act as a temporary trustee rather than an obsessed, anxious owner who lives in constant terror of loss.
This freedom from possessiveness leads directly to Shanta, deep, unshakeable internal peace.
Shanta is not a fragile silence that shatters the moment someone speaks rudely to you.
It is a massive, ocean-like stillness that remains calm no matter how violent the surface storms rage.
Think of how quiet the deep ocean floor remains while huge waves crash across the upper surface.
When you dismantle Ahankara, you no longer take personal offense at minor insults or temporary setbacks.
When you drop Darpa, you interact with every human being with authentic respect and humble understanding.
When you eliminate Krodha, your mind stops burning through precious energy on useless vengeance and resentment.
When you abandon Parigraha, your living space and mind become light, clean, and beautifully uncluttered.
This complete mental cleanup clears away all the artificial walls dividing you from universal reality.
You stop fighting against the natural flow of existence and align your energy with supreme truth.
This fitness for Brahman-realization is not an artificial reward given by someone outside of you.
It is the natural result of removing the heavy junk that was blocking your true nature all along.
Your mind becomes as clear as a spotless mirror, reflecting reality without distortion or bias.
You experience the absolute freedom of needing nothing external to feel completely whole.
This profound inner purity opens the door to ultimate spiritual mastery and endless peace.
You are now ready to step into the vast expanse of supreme divine consciousness.

devanagari:
ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षाति |
समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम् || ५४ ||
englishScript:
brahma-bhūtaḥ prasannātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣati
samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu mad-bhaktiṁ labhate parām (18.54)
translation: One who is established in Brahman becomes serene in self, neither grieving nor desiring. Viewing all beings with equal vision, such a soul attains supreme devotion unto Me.
sentences: What actually happens inside your day-to-day experience when you become Brahma-bhuta, fully established in universal consciousness?
First, you become Prasannatma, a soul radiant with cheerful, uncaused, and deep-seated inner joy.
This joy does not depend on winning a lottery, getting applause, or having ideal weather conditions outside.
It is like finding a freshwater spring inside your own house so you never have to beg for water outside again.
In this state, Na Shochati takes effect: you stop weeping, whining, and grieving over past losses and mistakes.
You realize that what is gone was merely a temporary wave that returned to the vast ocean of time.
Simultaneously, Na Kankshati takes effect: you stop burning with anxious future cravings for things you do not have.
When you know you are already whole and complete, the desperate urge to chase external validation vanishes.
You no longer live in a constant state of lack, feeling like a broken vessel that needs endless filling.
Instead, you look out at the world with Sama-drishti, seeing every single living being with equal value and respect.
Whether you look at a rich person, a poor person, a friend, or an enemy, you see the exact same underlying life essence.
Imagine looking at different gold ornaments—a ring, a necklace, or a crown—and realizing they are all just gold.
The shapes and names differ on the surface, but the core substance is identical in every single piece.
Seeing this underlying unity in all beings is not a forced moral duty; it becomes your natural way of perceiving.
From this clean foundation of equality and cheerfulness, you attain Para-bhakti, the highest form of supreme devotion.
Para-bhakti is not superficial emotional pleading or bargaining with the universe for personal favors.
It is a profound, mature love that flows naturally when all egoic barriers have completely dissolved.
You love the supreme source of life because you recognize your complete unity with it.
This devotion is untainted by fear, greed, or self-centered demands for personal gain.
Think of how a clean piece of iron naturally gets pulled toward a powerful magnet without any hesitation.
When your mind is freed from grief and desire, it gets pulled directly into supreme divine harmony.
You navigate daily challenges with an effortless smile because nothing can steal your inner wealth.
Past regrets no longer have the power to pull you back into depression or self-pity.
Future uncertainties no longer have the power to push you into panic or frantic anxiety.
You exist fully anchored in the present moment, experiencing life in its purest and richest form.
Your interactions with other people become gentle, compassionate, and deeply uplifting.
You radiate calm confidence that reassures everyone who comes near your quiet presence.
This is the golden state of emotional and spiritual resilience that cannot be shaken.
It marks the complete transition from a struggle-based life to a grace-filled existence.
By standing firm in this state, you become a living beacon of absolute truth and joy.
This high platform sets the stage for knowing the ultimate reality in total depth.

devanagari:
भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः |
ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम् || ५५ ||
englishScript:
bhaktyā mām abhijānāti yāvān yaś cāsmi tattvataḥ
tato māṁ tattvato jñātvā viśate tad-anantaram (18.55)
translation: Through supreme devotion one comes to know Me in truth, who and what I am. Then, knowing Me in ultimate reality, one enters immediately into My divine consciousness.
sentences: Let us examine how true devotion, Bhakti, becomes the ultimate microscope for knowing reality Tattvata, in its exact truth.
Many people think that intellectual debate alone can solve all mysteries of existence, but dry logic has strict limits.
Logic can measure the weight, chemical composition, and size of a violin, but it cannot measure the beauty of music.
Bhakti is the total opening of your heart and intellect, allowing you to experience the living truth directly.
Through Bhakti, you come to know Abhijayati: you recognize the supreme divinity as it truly exists in all dimensions.
You understand Yavan Yash Chāsmi, which means knowing both the manifest cosmic universe and the unmanifest eternal essence.
You see that the entire cosmos is not a random collision of dead matter, but an expression of supreme consciousness.
When you know reality Tattvata, all your false theories, superstitions, and narrow dogmas melt away instantly.
It is like switching on a bright light in a dark room where you previously mistook a simple rope for a dangerous snake.
The moment the light comes on, the snake vanishes and the simple rope is seen clearly for what it always was.
Knowing the supreme in truth removes all fear of death, isolation, and existential meaninglessness.
Once this Tattva-jnana, ultimate realization, takes place inside your mind, Vishate Tad-anantaram happens.
Vishate means you enter, merge, and integrate fully into that supreme state of infinite being.
There is no longer any painful separation between the individual observer and the universal reality.
Think of a single drop of rain falling into the vast, limitless ocean.
The drop does not get destroyed; rather, it expands its identity to become the entire ocean itself.
This merging is not a future event that happens only after your physical body drops away.
It is a present-moment realization that transforms your perception right here and right now.
Your daily work, conversations, and quiet moments become seamless expressions of divine awareness.
You stop searching for God in distant places because you see divine presence pulsating everywhere.
Every sight becomes a glimpse of the supreme, and every sound becomes a sacred melody.
This complete unity dissolves the last lingering shadows of doubt and intellectual confusion.
You no longer need external proofs or heavy arguments to believe in the ultimate reality.
Your own direct inner experience becomes the highest, most undeniable proof of truth.
This state of living union gives you absolute confidence, clarity, and unshakeable inner peace.
You move through the world with immense grace, serving others without any selfish expectation.
Your life becomes a clean instrument through which universal wisdom and love flow freely.
This is the climax of all knowledge, devotion, and action working together in perfect harmony.
It is the total realization of your true nature as eternal, pure, and infinitely free consciousness.
By reaching this understanding, you fulfill the deepest purpose of human existence.
You are now fully merged with the supreme source that sustains all worlds.

devanagari:
सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः |
प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम् || ५६ ||
englishScript:
sarva-karmāṇy api sadā kurvāṇo mad-vyapāśrayaḥ
mat-prasādād avāpnoti śāśvataṁ padam avyayam (18.56)
translation: Even while constantly performing all kinds of actions, one who takes exclusive refuge in Me reaches the eternal, imperishable state by My divine grace.
sentences: Here is a magnificent insight that liberates anyone working in the busy, high-stress modern world.
You do not need to run away to a quiet mountain cave or abandon your daily responsibilities to reach ultimate perfection.
The text explicitly says Sarva-karmani api sada kurvano: even while constantly performing all types of daily duties and actions.
Whether you are building houses, cooking meals, managing teams, or sweeping floors, your work itself can become your sanctuary.
The secret lever that transforms ordinary daily work into supreme spiritual discipline is Mad-vyapashrayah.
Mad-vyapashrayah means taking exclusive inner refuge in the supreme consciousness while you act.
Imagine a skilled actor performing on a theater stage, wearing a heavy costume and speaking dramatic lines.
On the outside, the actor plays the role with intense passion, but inside, they never forget their real name and identity.
They know it is all a play, so they do not get genuinely heartbroken or ruined when their character suffers on stage.
In the exact same way, you perform your daily duties with full dedication, but your mind stays anchored in supreme truth.
When you live with this inner orientation, Mat-prasadat comes into play: you receive divine grace and flow.
Prasada is not just a sweet offering; it is the natural clarity and peace that descends when egoic friction stops.
Through this grace, you attain Shashvatam Padam Avyayam, the eternal, imperishable, and unchanging state of freedom.
Shashvatam means timeless, completely untouched by the constant decay of physical years.
Avyayam means imperishable, a state that never degrades, rusts, or loses its intrinsic value.
Most human achievements in the physical world naturally wear out, break down, or get forgotten over time.
A empire crumbles, a machine breaks, and social fame fades away like mist in the morning sun.
But the inner state of Shashvata Pada remains completely untouched by physical decay.
By offering the results of every action to the supreme, you wipe out the sticky karma that usually binds people to stress.
You work with incredible efficiency because you are no longer paralyzed by fear of failure or greedy anxiety for success.
Your mind remains light, clear, and immensely creative under heavy operational pressure.
You view every challenge as a fascinating puzzle provided by life for your growth and learning.
Work stops being a painful burden you endure just to pay bills and survive.
It transforms into a joyful, dynamic expression of your inner freedom and gratitude.
You become a powerful force for good in your community without burning out or breaking down.
This master key proves that true renunciation is an internal state of consciousness, not an external escape.
You can stand in the middle of a noisy, chaotic market and remain as serene as a deep sage.
Every action becomes an offering of love, and every moment becomes a sacred opportunity.
This practical approach makes ultimate freedom accessible to every single working human being.
It bridges the gap between active daily duty and supreme spiritual enlightenment.
You are now living in the world while remaining completely untouched by its turmoil.

devanagari:
चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि सन्न्यस्य मत्परः |
बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव || ५७ ||
englishScript:
cetasā sarva-karmāṇi mayi sannyasya mat-paraḥ
buddhi-yogam upāśritya mac-cittaḥ satataṁ bhava (18.57)
translation: Mentally surrendering all activities unto Me, regarding Me as the supreme goal, and taking shelter of the yoga of intellect (Buddhi Yoga), keep your mind fixed continuously on Me.
sentences: Let us break down the internal mental mechanics of surrendering your actions using Cetasa Sarva-karmani Mayi Sannyasya.
Notice the crucial word Cetasa: this surrendering is done mentally, within the deep quiet space of your mind.
It does not mean throwing away your tools, quitting your job, or walking away from your family responsibilities.
It means holding an internal understanding that your body, brain, and talents are instruments of the cosmic whole.
When you work, you drop the micro-managing ego that claims 'I personally am doing all of this by my own isolated power.'
Instead, you recognize that your breath, heartbeat, thoughts, and muscles are all sustained by universal energy.
Being Mat-parah means making the supreme truth your ultimate reference point and highest priority in life.
Think of how a ship's captain uses the polar star to navigate through dark, stormy waters.
No matter how wildly the waves rock the ship, the captain keeps checking the fixed polar star to stay on course.
When you are Mat-parah, every choice you make is guided by your highest values rather than immediate selfish convenience.
To keep this navigation steady, you must rely on Buddhi-yogam Upashritya, taking shelter in the yoga of purified intellect.
Buddhi Yoga is the practice of using clear, unbiased discernment to guide your daily decisions.
It prevents your mind from falling into emotional traps, impulsive panic, and foolish self-deception.
With Buddhi Yoga, you evaluate situations calmly, choose the right path, and accept outcomes with equanimity.
The direct result of this practice is Mac-cittah Satatam Bhava: keeping your mind fixed continuously on supreme awareness.
Mac-cittah means having your consciousness soaked in divine presence during every single activity.
Whether you are writing a report, having a difficult conversation, or walking down a quiet street, your awareness stays centered.
Satatam means continuously, creating a smooth, unbroken flow of inner mindfulness throughout your day.
Imagine an oil stream being poured from one vessel to another; it flows in a continuous, unbroken thread without splashing.
That smooth oil-like flow is how your attention stays connected to supreme reality during daily living.
This constant connection eliminates the painful split between your spiritual life and your practical work life.
You no longer feel divided, exhausted, or hypocritical when moving between different roles.
Every moment becomes unified under one clear, noble purpose that energizes your entire system.
Your mind stops wasting precious cycles on worry, regret, envy, and useless overthinking.
You experience a massive increase in mental clarity, emotional stability, and operational efficiency.
This mental discipline transforms your daily routine into a living form of dynamic meditation.
You become remarkably resilient because your anchor is dropped in unshakeable truth rather than shifting circumstances.
This is how you master the art of continuous inner alignment amid constant external movement.
It turns every thought, word, and action into a beautiful thread in the tapestry of supreme consciousness.
By taking shelter in Buddhi Yoga, you safeguard your attention against all forms of mental distraction.
You are now ready to cross over every life obstacle with effortless grace and power.

devanagari:
मच्चित्तः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि |
अथ चेत्त्वमहङ्कारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि || ५८ ||
englishScript:
mac-cittaḥ sarva-durgāṇi mat-prasādāt tariṣyasi
atha cet tvam ahaṅkārān na śroṣyasi vinaṅkṣyasi (18.58)
translation: Fixing your mind on Me, you shall overcome all obstacles and difficulties by My grace. But if out of egoism you do not listen, you will perish.
sentences: Here is a blunt, uncompromising reality check about how your internal choices produce direct external consequences.
The verse promises Mac-cittah Sarva-durgani Mat-prasadat Tarishyasi: by keeping your mind centered on supreme reality, you will overcome all obstacles.
Sarva-durgani refers to all dangerous mountain passes, severe life crises, mental breakdowns, and complex external challenges.
When your mind is Mac-cittah, connected to universal wisdom, you receive intuitive guidance and clarity right when you need it.
You navigate dark, difficult situations with surprising calm because you are powered by something far bigger than your small ego.
Think of a traveler holding their strong guide's hand while walking through a dark, unfamiliar forest.
The traveler does not panic because they trust the immense strength and vision of the guide leading them.
Mat-prasadat means divine grace and natural cosmic alignment clear the way for you when your intent is pure.
Obstacles that seemed like giant impassable mountains suddenly turn into small stepping stones for your growth.
Now look closely at the sharp warning in the second half of the verse: Atha Cet Tvam Ahankarat Na Shrosyasi Vinanksyasi.
If, driven by Ahankara, false pride and arrogant self-reliance, you refuse to listen to truth, you will perish.
Vinanksyasi does not just mean physical death; it means the total breakdown of your peace, clarity, and purpose.
When ego takes over, you convince yourself that you know everything and do not need any higher wisdom.
You shut your eyes to reality, ignore constructive feedback, and make decisions based on stubborn vanity.
Imagine a ship captain ignoring weather warnings, smashing the compass, and sailing blindly straight into a violent hurricane.
That captain is guaranteed to shipwreck because stubborn arrogance cannot overrule the unyielding laws of nature.
Ego creates a massive blind spot that prevents you from seeing obvious dangers until it is far too late.
It makes you defensive, fragile, and terrified of being proven wrong in front of other people.
The choice presented here is utterly stark, crystal clear, and completely up to your personal free will.
Either you align your mind with universal truth and glide through life's storms with grace and ease,
Or you let your fragile ego drive the bus and crash straight into predictable disaster.
This principle operates with the mathematical precision of gravity; it cares nothing for your social status or titles.
If you jump off a tall building believing your ego makes you special, gravity will still pull you down instantly.
Respecting reality and listening to timeless wisdom is not weakness; it is the highest form of practical intelligence.
Humility opens your ears to hear truth, while arrogant pride seals your ears and ensures your downfall.
By choosing to drop egoic stubbornness, you protect your life from self-inflicted misery and ruin.
You open the door for supreme grace to guide every step of your personal journey.
This clear choice puts total responsibility for your destiny squarely back into your own hands.
It challenges you to examine where ego might still be blinding you in your current life decisions.
By choosing wisdom over pride, you guarantee your victory over every difficulty ahead.
Now let us examine how your internal nature forces action even when you try to run away.

devanagari:
यदहङ्कारमाश्रित्य न योत्स्य इति मन्यसे |
मिथ्यैष व्यवसायस्ते प्रकृतिं त्वां नियोक्ष्यति || ५९ ||
englishScript:
yad ahaṅkāram āśritya na yotsya iti manyase
mithyaiṣa vyavasāyas te prakṛtis tvāṁ niyokṣyati (18.59)
translation: If, driven by egoism, you think, "I will not fight," your resolve is completely futile; your internal psychological nature (Prakriti) will compel you to act regardless.
sentences: Let us explore a fascinating psychological illusion that tricks many people into making foolish, passive decisions.
Driven by sudden stress, emotional burnout, or moral confusion, you might say to yourself, 'I am quitting everything and walking away.'
The verse calls out this exact internal drama: Yad Ahankaram Ashritya Na Yotsya Iti Manyase.
You sit down in a fit of passive protest, believing that by refusing to participate, you are exercising supreme self-control.
Krishna looks right through this drama and declares: Mithya Esa Vyavasayaste, your resolution is completely false and futile!
Why is it futile? Because Prakritis Tvam Niyoksyati: your own deep psychological nature, Prakriti, will force you into action anyway.
You cannot turn off your internal engine simply by making a theatrical announcement that you are done fighting.
Think of a wild stallion tied to a post; it can pull against the rope all day, but its muscular nature will keep it moving.
Your personality is packed with Samskaras, deep psychological grooves and hardwired tendencies built over years of living.
If your underlying nature is built for leadership, justice, and active duty, sitting in quiet isolation will drive you insane.
Within three days of trying to sit passively, your internal fire will boil over and demand an outlet.
You will end up fighting small, petty battles in your quiet retreat because your active warrior energy has nowhere to go.
Trying to pretend you are a quiet, passive monk when your nature is a dynamic leader is complete self-deception.
It is like trying to force a high-powered race car engine to function quietly as a slow garden lawnmower.
The engine will overheat, shudder violently, and break down because it is operating completely against its design.
True peace comes from discovering your authentic internal design, Prakriti, and putting it to constructive use.
You cannot escape your duties by running away physically while your mind remains full of active desires.
Ego tricks you into thinking that quitting is a sign of high spirituality, when it is actually just cowardly evasion.
Recognizing your true nature saves you from wasting years on artificial, fake spiritual personas.
It brings absolute honesty to your self-analysis, forcing you to look at your real strengths and weaknesses.
Instead of suppressing your natural energy, you learn to channel it toward noble, selfless goals.
You realize that your active traits were given to you as specialized tools to fulfill your unique purpose in the world.
When you align your work with your genuine Prakriti, work feels natural, powerful, and deeply fulfilling.
Friction disappears because you are no longer rowing your boat against the powerful current of your own nature.
This insight exposes the complete foolishness of fake renunciation and lazy escapism.
It forces you to stop blaming external circumstances and take ownership of your built-in psychological drive.
You stop making dramatic excuses for avoiding hard work and step back into your rightful place of duty.
This clear realization strips away self-pity and restores your authentic personal power.
It teaches you to work with your nature rather than waging a foolish, exhausting war against it.
By understanding how Prakriti drives you, you gain true mastery over your behavioral choices.
Now let us look deeper into how these hardwired tendencies bind you from birth.

devanagari:
स्वभावजेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्मणा |
कर्तुं नेच्छसि यन्मोहात्करिष्यस्यवशोऽपि तत् || ६० ||
englishScript:
svabhāva-jena kaunteya nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇā
kartuṁ necchasi yan mohāt kariṣyasy avaśo ’pi tat (18.60)
translation: O son of Kunti, bound by your own inherent qualities born of your nature, that action which out of delusion you now wish to avoid, you will perform helplessly anyway.
sentences: Let us dig deeper into the concept of Svabhava-jena Karma, the actions born directly from your inherent psychological makeup.
Every single human being arrives with a specific set of built-in tendencies, talents, temperament, and emotional wiring.
This unique combination is your Svabhava, your intrinsic nature formed by your past conditioning and choices.
The text says Nibaddhah Svena Karmana: you are bound and tied to actions that match this underlying wiring.
Think of a seed planted in fertile soil; an apple seed cannot decide to grow into a banana tree, no matter how hard it tries.
Its internal code dictates that it will produce apples, branch out in a specific pattern, and bear specific fruit.
In the exact same way, your internal behavioral code drives your natural responses to life challenges.
When confused by Moha, emotional delusion and temporary panic, you might swear, 'I refuse to take on this big responsibility!'
You try to back out, step down, and hide in a corner to protect your immediate comfort.
But Krishna warns: Kartum Necchasi Yan Mohat Karisyasy Avaso 'pi Tat!
That very action which out of temporary delusion you now wish to avoid, you will end up performing helplessly anyway!
The word Avashah means helplessly or spontaneously, compelled by the massive momentum of your own nature.
When a crisis erupts and injustice occurs right in front of you, your built-in values will explode into action.
Your temporary pledge to stay passive will dissolve in a split second as your core nature takes total control.
Since you are going to perform the action anyway, why do it kicking, screaming, and suffering in self-pity?
Why not do it consciously, willingly, and with complete heroic alignment right from the very start?
Fighting against your own built-in duty only adds useless emotional friction and exhausting mental drama.
It is like a river trying to flow backward up a steep mountain; it wastes immense energy before inevitably turning around.
Accepting your natural duty with full awareness transforms reluctant struggle into magnificent masterwork.
You stop viewing your responsibilities as heavy punishments forced upon you by an unfair world.
Instead, you see them as the perfect arena designed specifically for your unique skills to shine.
This self-knowledge eliminates internal conflict and brings profound peace to your active life.
You no longer waste energy wishing you had someone else's talents, life role, or personality.
You take deep pride in mastering your own assigned path and executing it with absolute excellence.
This understanding frees you from the paralyzing guilt of trying to be someone you were never meant to be.
It allows you to focus 100% of your energy on expanding your genuine strengths.
You move from confused resistance to powerful, conscious cooperation with your life purpose.
This is the ultimate secret to living an authentic, high-impact human life without burning out.
By embracing your true nature, you turn mandatory duty into a glorious journey of self-realization.
You become an unstoppable force because your external work matches your internal wiring completely.
Now let us uncover the supreme operator sitting quietly behind the steering wheel of all existence.

devanagari:
ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति |
भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया || ६१ ||
englishScript:
īśvaraḥ sarva-bhūtānāṁ hṛd-deśe ’rjuna tiṣṭhati
bhrāmayan sarva-bhūtāni yantrārūḍhāni māyayā (18.61)
translation: The Supreme Lord dwells in the heart-region of all living beings, O Arjuna, causing all beings to revolve by His divine power (Maya), as if mounted on a machine.
sentences: Here is one of the most brilliant mechanical metaphors in all of global philosophical literature.
Ishvarah Sarva-bhutanam Hrid-dese 'rjuna Tisthati: the Supreme Controller sits right inside the heart-center of every single living being.
Notice where the supreme operator is located: not far away on a distant cloud in the sky, but right inside your own inner core!
What is this supreme controller actually doing inside us? Bhramayan Sarva-bhutani Yantrarudhani Mayaya!
It is causing all living beings to spin and move around as if they are mounted on a complex mechanical ride, Yantra.
Your physical body and mental apparatus are the Yantra, a highly sophisticated biological machine.
This biological machine is powered by Maya, the cosmic engine of nature that runs on energy, instincts, and psychological laws.
Think of a giant amusement park ride with mechanical horses moving up and down along fixed gear tracks.
The wooden horse feels like it is moving itself, but in reality, a central electric motor underneath drives the whole mechanism.
If the rider on the wooden horse believes they are personally steering the entire park, they are living in complete delusion.
Your body breathes, your heart pumps blood, your stomach digests food, and your brain fires neurons without your conscious effort.
Who is managing those millions of complex biological processes right now while you read these words?
It is the supreme intelligence, Ishvara, operating quietly through the automated machinery of nature.
Your small conscious ego is just a passenger sitting on top of this magnificent biological Yantra.
When you forget this truth, you take on massive, unnecessary anxiety, believing you must carry the entire cosmos on your shoulders.
You stress over things completely outside your control, exhausting your mind with foolish micromanagement.
Realizing that the supreme operator is running the underlying machinery instantly lifts that heavy mountain of stress off your chest.
You stop fighting the machine and learn to cooperate with the divine engineer sitting inside your heart.
This does not mean becoming a passive, brainless robot with no free will or personal responsibility.
It means aligning your small individual choices with the grand design of the universal engineer.
You handle the steering wheel of your attention while trusting the main engine to provide power and life.
This insight changes your relationship with your body, mind, and emotional states.
You observe physical sickness, mood swings, and aging as maintenance cycles of the outer Yantra, not your true self.
Your true self remains the peaceful observer, deeply connected with the supreme operator within.
This perspective brings instant relief, profound perspective, and incredible emotional freedom.
You move through life's complex situations with the relaxed confidence of a master driver.
You realize that every single human being around you is riding their own specialized Yantra, powered by the same source.
This understanding replaces judgmental anger with deep compassion for the struggles of other travelers.
It bridges the gap between mechanical science and deep spiritual realization.
By recognizing the operator within, you unlock the secret to effortless, joyful living.
Now let us see what total surrender to this supreme internal operator actually looks like.

devanagari:
तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत |
तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम् || ६२ ||
englishScript:
tam eva śaraṇaṁ gaccha sarva-bhāvena bhārata
tat-prasādāt parāṁ śāntiṁ sthānaṁ prāpsyasi śāśvatam (18.62)
translation: Surrender unto Him completely with all your being, O descendant of Bharata. By His grace you will attain supreme peace and the eternal abode.
sentences: Once you realize that a supreme operator sits inside your heart running the universe, what is the smartest move you can make?
The text gives the ultimate operational directive: Tam Eva Sharanam Gaccha Sarva-bhavena Bharata!
Surrender unto that supreme inner controller completely, with every single aspect of your being, Sarva-bhavena.
Sarva-bhavena means total commitment: your intellect, your emotions, your actions, your plans, and your silent moments.

It means handing over the master steering wheel of your life to the divine wisdom within you.
Think of a patient who has been struggling with a severe illness for years, trying useless home remedies and internet tips.
Finally, they walk into the clinic of the world's greatest specialist doctor and say, 'I surrender completely to your treatment plan.'
They stop arguing, follow every instruction precise to the letter, and let the master doctor heal them.
That total trust and complete cooperation is the exact essence of Sharanam, authentic spiritual surrender.
What happens when you surrender with Sarva-bhavena? Tat-prasadat Param Shanti Sthanam Prapsyasi Shashvatam!
By that supreme grace, you attain Param Shanti, absolute, unshakeable, and ultimate peace.
This is not a temporary calm that disappears when bad news arrives in the mail.
It is an eternal sanctuary, Shashvatam Sthanam, a permanent dwelling place of consciousness that can never be destroyed.
When you surrender your small, anxious ego, you stop fighting against the infinite intelligence of the universe.
You stop trying to force open closed doors with brute willpower and learn to read the subtle signals of life.
You discover that when you get out of your own way, life flows with unbelievable efficiency and grace.
Solutions to complex problems appear spontaneously, resources arrive right on time, and key relationships fall into place.
You no longer suffer from severe burnout because you are no longer trying to power your life on small ego battery power.
You are plugged directly into the main power grid of universal cosmic energy.
This surrender requires immense courage because your fragile ego hates letting go of control.
Ego loves the dramatic illusion that it is struggling heroically against a hostile world.
Surrender shatters that tragic drama and reveals that the universe was supporting you lovingly all along.
You experience the absolute sweetness of complete trust, dropping all chronic worry and sleep-stealing anxiety.
Your heart becomes light, clean, and filled with radiant joy that infects everyone around you.
You live as a dedicated steward of divine energy, acting with supreme skill while remaining totally unattached.
This is the ultimate refuge where all human suffering, confusion, and fear permanently come to an end.
It provides an unbreakable foundation for your mind, regardless of how chaotic the world becomes.
By taking complete shelter in the supreme within, you secure your place in eternal truth.
Your journey transforms into a continuous celebration of divine peace and unshakeable mastery.
Now pay close attention to how Krishna respects your personal freedom right after delivering this supreme wisdom.

devanagari:
इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया |
विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु || ६३ ||
englishScript:
iti te jñānam ākhyātaṁ guhyād guhyataraṁ mayā
vimṛśyaitad aśeṣeṇa yathecchasi tathā kuru (18.63)
translation: Thus has wisdom more secret than all secrets been declared to you by Me. Reflect upon it deeply in its entirety, and then do as you choose.
sentences: Here is one of the most stunning, breathtaking demonstrations of intellectual freedom in the entire history of human thought.
Krishna has just explained the deepest mechanics of existence, work, mind control, and divine realization.
He calls this teaching Guhyad Guhyataram: knowledge that is more secret and profound than all other hidden secrets.
It is called secret not because it was hidden under lock and key in a dark basement to keep people out.
It is secret because subtle truth cannot be seen by a noisy, superficial mind that only looks at surface appearances.
You have to refine your intellect to perceive these subtle internal mechanics, just like you need a microscope to see tiny cells.
After delivering this mind-boggling manual of life, what does the supreme teacher say?
Does He issue a terrifying threat like, 'If you do not obey me right now, you will burn in hell forever'?
No! He utters the ultimate charter of personal freedom: Vimrsyaitad Asesena Yathecchasi Tatha Kuru!
Reflect upon everything I have taught you deeply, thoroughly, and in its complete entirety—and then do whatever you choose!
Take a moment to absorb the staggering beauty and respect embedded in those words.
True spiritual wisdom never coerces, brains-washes, manipulates, or forces anyone into blind submission.
It lays out the precise laws of reality with crystal clarity, like an expert showing you how gravity or electricity works.
The expert says, 'Here are the live wire mechanics; if you touch it safely with insulation, you get power; if you touch it bare-handed, you get shocked.'
'Now that you understand the exact physics, the choice of how to handle the wire is entirely yours.'
Vimrsya means analyzing the principles with sharp critical thinking, testing them against your real-life experience.
Asesena means examining every single detail without leaving out awkward questions or suppressing doubt.
You are explicitly encouraged to be a relentless seeker who investigates reality with total intellectual honesty.
Only when you understand truth through your own careful reflection does knowledge become real power.
Blind belief accepted out of fear or social pressure is fragile and breaks down during the first serious crisis.
Realized wisdom, tested through your own deep thinking, becomes an unshakeable inner compass for life.
This verse honors your human intellect and celebrates your fundamental free will as a conscious being.
It puts the steering wheel of your destiny completely into your own hands without any manipulative guilt.
You are not a helpless puppet being bossed around by a tyrant in the sky.
You are a conscious partner in existence, gifted with the freedom to choose your path and reap its natural results.
This incredible freedom inspires deep obsession to study, master, and verify every single layer of this teaching.
It transforms learning from a forced, boring chore into an exhilarating, self-driven adventure of exploration.
You feel an intense curiosity to test these mental models in your daily work, relationships, and quiet reflection.
By honoring your freedom, the teaching invites you to step up and take full responsibility for your life.
It puts you in the driver's seat of your own consciousness, empowering you to live with deep purpose and total clarity.
Now let us prepare for the ultimate, most confidential summary statement of the entire Bhagavad Gita.

devanagari:

You realize you are an infinitely cherished soul of the supreme source, supported at every single moment.

It opens your mind completely to receive the final instruction without any remaining defensive barriers.
Think of a loving mentor pulling their trusted student aside right before a big life journey to give them the ultimate family key.

It condenses all philosophy, yoga practices, and ethical rules into one clear, beautiful path of action.
It requires no complex scholastic jargon or years of tedious academic debate to put into immediate practice.
It is simple enough for anyone to embrace, yet profound enough to baffle the world's greatest philosophers.
By preparing your attention for this supreme message, you stand on the threshold of complete liberation.
Your curiosity reaches an all-time high as you lean in close to hear the ultimate directive.
You feel a powerful desire to uncover this final layer and master its practical application in your life.
This intimate bond between the seeker and the supreme source forms the heart of true spiritual transformation.
It guarantees that you are never alone, never abandoned, and always guided toward ultimate perfection.
It provides an unshakeable foundation for navigating the uncertainties of human existence.
Now let us open our hearts to absorb this supreme declaration in its full, majestic glory.
Now let us hear the precise, four-fold action plan that constitutes this supreme secret.

devanagari:

englishScript:

First directive: Man-mana Bhava—fill your mind with awareness of the supreme reality in every single situation.

Think of a musician playing an instrument while keeping their internal ear tuned perfectly to the foundational drone chord.
Second directive: Mad-bhakto Bhava—direct your deep love and heartfelt devotion toward the supreme presence.
Stop squandering your deepest affection on temporary, fickle objects that bring inevitable heartbreak and disappointment.
Anchor your love in the eternal source that will never abandon, betray, or fade away from you.
Third directive: Mad-yaji Bhava—make every single work, task, and action a sacred sacrifice offered to the supreme.
When you cook, cook with love; when you clean, clean with care; when you work, serve with absolute excellence.
Every action stops being a selfish grab for personal profit and becomes a beautiful, generous gift to life.
Fourth directive: Mam Namaskuru—bow down your proud ego before the universal presence in all beings.
Namaskaru means replacing arrogant self-importance with humble reverence for the divine life pulsating everywhere.
When you bow internally, you shatter the rigid, defensive shell of Ahankara that keeps you feeling small and isolated.
Look at the absolute, unbreakable guarantee given right after these four simple steps!
Mam Evaisyasi Satyam Te Pratijane Priyo 'si Me: You will undoubtedly come to Me alone; I promise you truly, for you are dearly beloved to Me!
This is a solemn, divine contract signed and sealed by the supreme authority of the cosmos.
It is not a vague 'maybe' or a conditional possibility dependent on luck or social standing.
It is a mathematical certainty: follow these four simple internal alignments, and absolute realization is guaranteed.

You do not need money, high social status, complex academic degrees, or physical strength to practice these steps.
You can practice Man-mana while working, Mad-bhakto while loving, Mad-yaji while acting, and Namaskuru while interacting.
This simple framework integrates your entire personality—intellect, emotions, action, and ego—into total harmony.
It leaves no part of your daily life left out in the cold as 'unspiritual' or useless.
Your whole day transforms into a seamless, joyful journey of continuous spiritual growth and mastery.
You experience incredible mental clarity, deep emotional security, and effortless operational skill.
The constant friction of chasing selfish desires vanishes, replaced by the deep peace of divine alignment.
You realize that ultimate spiritual perfection is not far away in time or space, but right here in your current practice.
By taking this divine promise to heart, you gain unshakeable confidence in your ultimate destiny.
This four-fold path guarantees that your mind remains calm, clear, and immensely powerful under all life circumstances.
It establishes an unbreakable bridge between your daily activities and eternal supreme awareness.
Now let us examine the ultimate climax verse of the entire Bhagavad Gita, the famous Charama Shloka.

devanagari:
सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज |

englishScript:

translation: Abandoning all varieties of duty and conditional reliance, take refuge in Me alone. I will deliver you from all sinful reactions and bondages; do not grieve.
sentences: This is the world-famous Charama Shloka, the absolute ultimate crescendo and final grand declaration of the Bhagavad Gita.

The verse begins with a radical directive: Sarva-dharman Parityajya—abandon all varieties of conditional duties, rules, and self-made reliances!

Absolutely not! It means dropping your anxious reliance on superficial, external religious rituals, social formulas, and egoic self-righteousness.

You think, 'If I follow this specific ritual, wear these clothes, or belong to this group, I am guaranteed safety.'
Krishna says: drop all those artificial, fragile crutches and step into direct, unmediated connection with the supreme source!
Mam Ekam Sharanam Vraja: take exclusive, total refuge in Me alone, the one underlying reality of all existence!
Stop dividing your trust among a hundred temporary things—money, social titles, temporary praise, and fragile human promises.
Anchor your entire security in the one imperishable source that sustains all cosmic universes.
When you take this total leap of trust, listen to the supreme promise that immediately responds: Aham Tvam Sarva-papebhyo Moksayisyami!
I will personally deliver and liberate you from all sinful reactions, past karmic bondages, guilt, and psychological burdens!
All the accumulated dirt, mistakes, regrets, and subconscious guilt of your past melt away instantly in the fire of total surrender.
It is like turning on a bright spotlight inside a dark cave that has been pitch-black for ten thousand years.
The darkness does not leave slowly over ten thousand years; it vanishes in one single microsecond the moment light appears!
In the exact same way, total surrender to the supreme source burns away all past karmic baggage instantly.
The verse concludes with the two most comforting words in all scripture: Ma Shucah—do not grieve, do not fear, and do not worry any longer!
Wipe away your tears, drop your heavy mental burdens, and stand up with calm, radiant, heroic confidence.
You are fully protected, completely forgiven, immensely loved, and permanently liberated by divine grace.
This Charama Shloka is the ultimate safety net for every struggling, imperfect human being.
It proves that no matter how many past mistakes you have made, complete redemption and perfection are instantly available right now.
You do not need years of painful penance to earn love; you simply need to let go of egoic resistance and surrender to truth.
This realization brings a wave of immense emotional release, profound relief, and deep inner joy.
Your mind experiences absolute freedom from existential guilt, anxiety, and paralyzing self-doubt.
You step into your daily duties powered by divine grace rather than fragile human ego strength.
This master verse represents the absolute summit of spiritual wisdom, love, and ultimate liberation.
It is the eternal guarantee of ultimate victory for anyone who takes refuge in supreme truth.
By anchoring your heart in this Charama Shloka, you master the ultimate secret of human existence.
You step into the world as a radiant beacon of divine love, peace, and ultimate freedom.
Now let us examine the strict qualifications required for sharing and receiving this sacred wisdom.

devanagari:
इदं ते नातपस्काय नाभक्ताय कदाचन |
न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति || ६७ ||
englishScript:
idaṁ te nātapaskāya nābhaktāya kadācana

translation: This confidential knowledge must never be explained to one who lacks austerity, nor to one who is devoid of devotion, nor to one who is unwilling to listen, nor to one who harbors malice toward Me.
sentences: Why does a master teacher place strict ground rules on who can receive deep, transformative wisdom?

Second category: Na Abhaktaya—never speak this to one who is devoid of Bhakti, lacking basic humility, love, and open-hearted trust.

Fourth category: Na Cha Mam Yo 'bhyasuyati—never share this with one who harbors active malice, envy, or hatred toward divine truth.

Throwing deep spiritual secrets before malicious cynics only produces useless arguments and hostile negativity.
Think of a doctor taking precious, life-saving medicine and dumping it down a dirty drain where it helps nobody.
Wisdom is extremely precious fuel; it should be shared only where there is a clean engine ready to burn it productively.
Protecting sacred knowledge from misuse is not arrogant elitism; it is basic practical wisdom and energy management.
It ensures that high-level insights are preserved in their purity for genuine seekers who are truly ready to transform.
When a seeker shows real Tapas, genuine Bhakti, eager willingness to listen, and deep respect, then open the floodgates of wisdom!
This rule teaches you to discern who is ready for deep conversations and who needs simple, surface-level interaction.
You stop wasting your time arguing with arrogant internet trolls or cynical people who just want to fight.
You save your highest insights for sincere conversations with friends who truly desire to grow and learn.
This boundary keeps your own mind clean, peaceful, and protected from useless ideological battles.
It respects the natural timing of every human soul's unique journey of growth and awakening.
People wake up when they are ready; you cannot force a flower bud to blossom by violently tearing open its petals.
By following these guidelines, you preserve the high value and dignity of profound spiritual truth.
You become a wise dispenser of knowledge, sharing light exactly where it can take firm root and flourish.
This operational discipline ensures that wisdom continues to illuminate human minds without dilution or corruption.
It reminds us to cultivate our own internal readiness so we remain fit to receive higher wisdom continuously.
This careful filtering protects the sacred dignity of knowledge from being dragged down into futile arguments.
It reminds us that genuine growth requires a willing heart, a humble mind, and a disciplined life.
Now let us look at the immense spiritual glory promised to those who share this wisdom with sincere seekers.

devanagari:

englishScript:

translation: One who teaches this supreme secret to My devotees, demonstrating pure devotion unto Me, shall undoubtedly come to Me without any doubt.
